project.name: Style Rip Test PS1
project.description: Single 5s news scene, 1 host, PS1 low-poly aesthetic ripped from IG reel

source.prompt: STYLE: Late 90s PS1 video game 3D render. Low-poly geometry with low-resolution pixelated photographic textures and no anti-aliasing (visible jaggies on every edge). Flat vertex lighting, no dynamic shadows, bright unlit shaders for neon signs. Match the look in the reference images exactly — same polygon count, same pixelated texture quality, same flat lighting, same vivid neon palette. SCENE: A low-poly news studio at night, modeled like a PS1-era video game environment. A single news anchor sits behind a chunky polygonal news desk. The anchor is a low-poly 3D character: blocky proportions, simple polygonal hair, pixelated face texture with painted-on features, wearing a vivid red blazer over a white shirt. Behind the anchor, a wall of low-poly TV monitors glowing with abstract neon signage and a 'BREAKING NEWS' sign in vivid red unlit shader. Static deep navy starry skybox visible through a window on the side. ACTION: The camera is locked off. The anchor looks at camera and says with deadpan delivery: 'Welcome to the news. Tonight, everything is fine.' AUDIO: clean close-mic'd dialogue, slight retro low-fi compression, faint synth news-jingle sting at the very start, distant night ambience.
